page: Amazon Web Services m8a.medium is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor running at a clock frequency of 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 1 dedicated vCPU comprising 1 physical core and 1 thread per core, accompanied by 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 4.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, yielding a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware virtualization and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, with no GPU hardware provisioned.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capability coupled with expected scaling limitations inherent to a single-core instance. Stress-ng single-core performance registers 3762.69, positioning the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, identical to its multi-core stress-ng score due to the single-core topology. Geekbench single-core performance is similarly in the top tier at 2750.0, backed by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 41.2 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 18.08 GB/sec. Conversely, total system throughput tests such as Geekbench multi-core (2767.0) and PassMark CPU (3490.66) fall into the lower 25 percent. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth register at 47.43 GB/sec and 34.42 GB/sec respectively, reflecting middle-tier performance.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC core provides high computational capability per thread without the variance typical of burstable instances. The absence of local disk drives requires architectural accommodation for network storage latency, and the 1 Gbps network baseline is optimized for low-volume throughput. Static web serving reaches 6.77 GB/sec, while Redis operations measure 4.17 million operations per second. The m8a.medium is suited for lightweight microservices, single-threaded processing pipelines, utility scripts, internal continuous integration workers, and entry-level development environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8a.medium is an entry-level general-purpose instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the server features 1 dedicated vCPU with 1 physical core running at 4.5 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of DDR5 system memory at 6 GHz. The instance includes 4 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instruction extensions, but bundles no local storage or GPU accelerators. Baseline network throughput is 1 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance, scoring 2750.0 on Geekbench and reaching 41.2 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core throughput is constrained by the single-core boundary, placing overall multi-threaded metrics in the bottom quartile. The m8a.medium is suited for lightweight web serving, isolated microservices, background task execution, and non-concurrent processing workloads.
